backup-restore.heading: Save, transfer and restore your project.
backup-restore.intro: Export a full project or selected components as a ZIP backup. Keep a copy away from your Pi, upload a compatible snapshot and review what will change before restoring.
bullets: Create full baselines or small component snapshots.
Download and upload versioned project archives.
Preview replacements with an automatic recovery snapshot.

hardware.heading: Connect and configure your hardware.
hardware.intro: Set up switches, coils and lights using the hardware editor. Give each connection a name, choose its function and configure the appropriate output settings.
bullets: Map switches, coils and lights to your hardware.
Configure coil pulse, hold and safety limits.
Deploy supported hardware settings to the ESP32-S3.

rule-editor.heading: Create your own game rules.
rule-editor.intro: Use the rule editor to decide what happens when switches are triggered. Create scoring rules, combinations and multipliers, and control how your machine responds during gameplay.
bullets: Create rules using events, conditions and actions.
Set up scoring, combinations and multipliers.
Run supported hardware rules directly on the ESP32-S3.

lighting.heading: Design your playfield lighting.
lighting.intro: Arrange lights on a visual representation of your playfield and create lighting effects for different events and game modes. Preview your designs as you work.
bullets: Position lights on your playfield layout.
Create lighting effects and scenes.
Preview your lighting before deploying supported configurations.

media.title: Media
media.heading: Add sound and displays to your game.
media.intro: Manage sound effects, music and display content from Pinball CTL. Create scenes for your backglass and other displays, including custom animated content built with Godot.
bullets: Upload and organise your sound library.
Configure audio cues and playback.
Create display scenes and integrate Godot content.

playfield-layout.heading: Build and test without a complete machine.
playfield-layout.intro: Arrange your layout in Playfield, open Live View to test configured inputs and preview lighting, and watch counters and timers in Rules State. It's useful when developing a new game, experimenting with layouts or working on your project before all the hardware is installed. Connected event-path testing requires an ESP32-S3; physical outputs and hardware timing still need testing on the real machine.
bullets: Create and work with a visual playfield layout.
Trigger configured inputs and preview lighting responses.
Test the connected event path when an ESP32-S3 is available.

performance.heading: See what your machine is doing.
performance.intro: Monitor events, check communication between the Raspberry Pi and ESP32-S3, and investigate problems using built-in performance tools and logs.
bullets: Monitor event activity and delivery times.
Check queues and controller communication.
View logs to help diagnose problems.
